relevance_note: Family case report of two affected Japanese siblings with a heterozygous TNFAIP3 frameshift: 'This heterozygous C200A fs*16 mutation was present in the patient’s younger sister, who showed similar symptoms.'
method_note: Read the whole paper, including the converted supplementary laboratory table (Table S1), by hand; a short Python script assembled the JSON and copied the two supplementary-table spans (CRP, ANA) by regex to keep exact whitespace, then verified spans and fields. Scope: 4 rows: the proband ('patient', rule 5; the paper calls him 'the patient' and 'the proband'), his younger sister (carrier, affected), his mother (affected, deceased, never tested; no variant row) and his father (tested negative; no variant row). The 'younger brothers of the proband without symptoms' were neither tested ('Sequence analysis was not possible') nor affected and their number is not given, so they get no rows. Contradictions/ambiguities in the paper: (1) cDNA description differs between text ('C596_598 del A') and Fig. 1 legend ('c597-598 T deletion'); the text form is recorded in variant_original_string and cdna_hgvs_as_stated. (2) Variant class: called a frameshift (text and legend) but 'a novel heterozygous missense mutation' in the Discussion; recorded 'frameshift'. (3) Protein printed as 'Cys200Alafsx16', 'C200Afs*16' and 'C200A fs*16'; first form recorded. (4) Inheritance left 'not reported' per v4: father tested negative, authors only 'suggest' maternal derivation and the mother (affected, deceased) was not tested. (5) Timeline: 17-year-old at referral with a 3-year history, then admitted 'Three years later'; age at last evaluation is therefore unclear and left 'not reported' (onset 'at 14 years old' from the Discussion). (6) Text says 'no abnormalities except elevated levels of C-reactive protein' yet also reports positive ANA and raised cytokines, and Table S1 shows other out-of-range values (e.g. serum amyloid A); these general statements were not used to exclude cytopenia or other checklist items. Functional (immunoblot) evidence was obtained on the proband's PBMCs only; it is attached to both carriers' variant rows because the field describes the variant. 'Neither genital ulcer nor uveitis was confirmed' was recorded as excluded for genital ulcers and uveitis; the checklist item 'uveitis or other ocular inflammation' stays 'not reported' (narrow vs broad rule). The sister's features are given only as 'similar symptoms' (no specific feature), so she has no phenotypic_features rows; the father is described only as 'unaffected'/'healthy', so no feature rows. Ethnicity 'Japanese' for sister, mother and father comes from the family-level statement. HPO IDs given only where confident.

functional_evidence_statement.value: immunoblot of the proband's PBMCs: reduced wild-type A20 protein expression at baseline and after TNF-α stimulation, and reduced cytosolic IκB-α after TNF-α stimulation (accelerated IκB-α degradation) versus a healthy control
span: Wild-type A20 protein expression was reduced in patient-derived PBMCs compared with those from the healthy subject at baseline and after TNF-α stimulation.

cytosolic inhibitor of nuclear factor kappa B alpha (IκB-α) protein levels were reduced in patient-derived PBMCs after stimulation with TNF-α, whereas IκB-α protein levels were unchanged in control PBMCs.
These findings suggest that IκB-α degradation was accelerated by TNF-α stimulation in PBMCs isolated from the patient.
